title: When God Has to Pull Us Out

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: With the coming of dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, "Hurry! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away when the city is punished." When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and of his two daughters and led them safely out of the city, for the Lord was merciful to them. - Gen 19:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most tender and revealing verses in the chapter. The angels urge Lot to flee - and "he hesitated." With fire about to fall, with his life and family at stake, Lot lingers. His heart was still tangled up in Sodom. So the angels physically "grasped his hand" and the hands of his family, and dragged them out to safety. And Scripture gives the reason: "for the Lord was merciful to them."

What a picture of grace. Lot didn't even flee well. He dithered, clung, delayed. And God's mercy did not wait for him to get it right. When Lot would not move, grace took him by the hand and pulled him out anyway. Our salvation often depends far more on God's grip on us than our grip on Him.

Why did Lot hesitate? Because part of his heart still belonged to the very place that was about to be destroyed. We can be like that - clinging to things that are killing us, reluctant to let go even of what we know is doomed.

But here is the gospel comfort: "the Lord was merciful to them." When we hesitate, when our hearts are divided, when we cannot even flee properly, God's mercy reaches out and takes hold of us. He is "the author and finisher of our faith" (Heb 12:2). If God has ever had to pull you out of something by the hand, that was not weakness on your part alone - it was mercy on His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you clinging to something that is not good for you?
- Can you thank God for the times His mercy pulled you out when you hesitated?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Merciful Lord, thank You for the times You took me by the hand and pulled me out when I hesitated. Where my heart still clings to what is doomed, loosen my grip, and hold onto me by Your grace.
Amen.
